brief: RIPPLE TANK: a physics lab bench simulating the 2D wave equation in real time (finite differences; GPU via WebGL2 float textures preferred, CPU typed-array fallback around 300x200). Users place oscillating point sources (drag to move; slider or wheel sets frequency and phase), draw walls and erase them, and pick experiments: Young's double slit, single-slit diffraction, two-source interference, a parabolic reflector focusing plane waves, refraction through a paintable shallow-water region (slower wave speed) acting as a lens or prism, and a moving source showing the Doppler effect and a bow wave when it moves faster than the wave speed. Absorbing boundaries (damping sponge layer) so waves do not reflect off the tank edges. Rendering: shaded water surface (height to normal to lighting) plus an Intensity view showing time-averaged amplitude squared so interference fringes become crisp bands; colour-blind-safe palettes. Live, correct readouts: wavelength = v/f in cells and on the tank's millimetre scale, and for the double-slit preset the predicted fringe spacing (approximately lambda*L/d) drawn as tick marks on a screen line so users can compare prediction with simulation. Controls: play/pause, step, speed, damping, frequency, view mode, presets, clear. Use a CFL-stable time step. The first frame must show a running double-slit pattern (pre-run before display).
